wy_medicine_bow_peak_area.blurb: Laramie's nearest alpine climbing, on the slabs just below Medicine Bow Peak in the Snowy Range. Most of the 26 climbs are trad, with a handful of alpine routes, some short ice lines and a couple of mountaineering objectives. Rock climbs run from easy fifth class up to the 5.11 range, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.10; the ice is WI1 to WI3. The quartzite is slick, low in angle and loose, routes can reach about five pitches, and gear is sparse enough that runouts come with the harder lines. Everything starts above treeline near 10,500 feet and the walls face east, so expect a serious, committing day with real rockfall potential rather than a casual crag outing.
wy_medicine_bow_peak_area.approach: A faint path leaves the Lake Marie picnic area through trees and climbs onto a scree slope. From there it is cross-country over talus to the foot of the slabs.

wy_toaster_wall_the.blurb: A small sport wall in the Laramie Range of southeast Wyoming, at roughly 7,500 feet. Nearly all of its 26 routes are bolted, with a single trad line, and the rock is clean, mostly vertical gneiss that rewards steady movement. The grade spread leans hard: a few routes in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, a modest middle in the 5.10s and low 5.11s, and the biggest cluster at 5.12, with several 5.13s on top. Moderate climbers will find only a few warm-up options, so this suits people already climbing 5.11 or above. Routes are fairly short, and the wall sits well away from town on a remote, dirt-road drive.

wy_crazy_woman_cliff.blurb: The main developed wall of Crazy Woman Crags, in the Eastern Big Horns above high meadows near 8,500 feet. This is steep, well-featured dolomite with 25 sport routes and one trad line, mostly in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, plus a few 5.10s and a handful of 5.13s. Easier climbers get little here beyond a couple of 5.9s. Altitude keeps summer days pleasant, and mornings and evenings stay comfortable even in the hottest months. Trees along the base give some shade, and the far left end holds shade best, while the right side stands open to the sun. The walk from the road is only a few minutes.

wy_cascade_canyon.blurb: A broad climbing zone inside Grand Teton National Park, rising from the shores of Jenny Lake into the canyon between the Teton giants. The 26 listed lines are a mix of alpine and trad routes, a cluster of boulder problems from VB-level up to V7, and one ice route. Rock routes run from about 5.8 through the 5.10s, with a few at 5.11 and 5.12, and many are multi-pitch. Approaches are fairly short and gentle for the Tetons, reached by a boat shuttle across the lake or a lakeside walk, and the walls get plenty of sun. The setting beneath the high peaks is as much a draw as the climbing.

wy_2_fossil_hill_central.blurb: The first stretch of cliff you meet on the trail up at Fossil Hill, a high sport zone above Sinks Canyon near Lander, at about 8,800 feet. All 25 routes are bolted, tall and clean, with mostly vertical climbing and steeper bulges higher up. This is hard-climber terrain: most routes fall at 5.12, with a good group at 5.11 and a couple at 5.13, and only one or two lines below that. Climbs are long, typically needing eight to twelve bolts. The hill faces west and can get warm around midday, so cooler fall days and late summer evenings are the favored times to visit.

wy_first_tier.blurb: The lowest and largest level of the Full Tilt wall at The Joint in Sinks Canyon, near Lander, at roughly 7,500 feet. It is a steep, overhanging, streaked cliff with 25 bolted routes, and it is where sport climbing at this wall began. The grades run hard: only a few climbs sit below 5.11, a solid group are at 5.11, and the largest numbers fall at 5.12 and 5.13, with a couple of harder lines beyond. It suits strong sport climbers working on power and endurance and offers little for beginners. The flagship line is regarded as one of the best of its grade in the Lander area.
wy_first_tier.approach: Follow the trail up through talus, passing beneath the blocky Mr. Big Shot wall, to reach the foot of the tiered, overhanging cliff.

wy_moss_cave_face_dancer.blurb: A sport crag in Sinks Canyon above the Popo Agie River near Lander, at about 7,300 feet, pairing a steep cave with a clean vertical face to its right. Routes are single-pitch, around 60 feet. The face carries the friendlier climbing, mostly 5.10 to 5.11a, plus a few easy lines near 5.5. The cave holds the hard stuff, up through 5.13. In between, there is a good dose of 5.11 and 5.12. The cave stays cool and shady, which helps on hot afternoons, though it seeps now and then and is a bit less tidy than some neighbors. The river noise echoes loudly inside.

wy_maze_aka_amaze_ing_the.blurb: An outlying formation at Vedauwoo, near Laramie, at about 7,850 feet, west of the central crags and reached on foot. It earns its name from the chimneys, hidden corridors and narrow passages that several climbs start in. Of the 24 routes, most are single-pitch trad, with two bolted lines and one top-rope. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.11, with a healthy middle at 5.9 and 5.10 and a handful of easier outings in the 5.6 to 5.8 range. Expect granite, crack and chimney climbing with a quirky, adventurous feel, and generally more solitude than the busy main areas.
